headline: South Asia: 'Everything necessary will be done': Military spokesman reaffirms Pakistan's right to self-defence against Afghanistan-based terrorism
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: 'Everything necessary will be done': Military spokesman reaffirms Pakistan's right to self-defence against Afghanistan-based terrorism.
- Australia: School and nuclear facility hit in latest wave of Russian strikes.
- Western Russia: Ukrainian forces strike drone site and Russian arms depot, destroy Rubicon warehouses.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Navy Expeditionary Combat Command rebranded to reflect warfare evolution.
- Military Times, 3 hours ago: Navy Expeditionary Combat Command rebranded to reflect warfare evolution.
CNO Adm. Daryl Caudle announced that the Navy Expeditionary Combat Command will now be known as Commander, Navy Expeditionary Forces.
- Military Times, 2 hours ago: Boeing adds to big week with first full-rate Grey Wolf helicopter order.
The U.S. Air Force awarded Boeing a roughly $85 million contract for four more MH-139A Grey Wolf helicopters, with the first under full-rate production.
- Military Times, 23 hours ago: Hegseth announces new four-star command for autonomous warfare.
The new Autonomous Warfare Command, or AutoWarCom, aims to address an acquisition system that isn't keeping pace with the speed of technological change.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Samuda warns tougher water curbs coming.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 15 hours ago: Samuda warns tougher water curbs coming.
Water Minister Matthew Samuda is warning that tougher water restrictions are coming as Jamaica continues to grapple with a crippling drought, signalling an escalation in the Government’s response to the prolonged dry spell. The minister gave the dire update during yesterday’s post-Cabinet press briefing at Jamaica House in St Andrew. The National Water Commission (NWC) imposed water prohibition orders on August 17, restricting the use of NWC-supplied water for non-essential activities such as watering lawns, washing vehicles and refilling pools across seven parishes.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Argentine rugby player murdered in Paris honored by French league.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 2 hours ago: Argentine rugby player murdered in Paris honored by French league.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Ukrainian forces strike drone site and Russian arms depot, destroy Rubicon warehouses.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Ukrainian forces strike drone site and Russian arms depot, destroy Rubicon warehouses.
Ukraine's General Staff has confirmed strikes on a drone launch site, arms depot and the destruction of Rubicon unit UAV warehouses.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Lithuanian president on Russian nuclear threat letter: reckless remarks becoming more frequent.
Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda has said he is not surprised by Russia's letter to NATO threatening nuclear strikes over Kaliningrad Oblast.
- The Moscow Times, 4 hours ago: Putin Says World Is Living Through a Dangerous Moment, Warns West Not to Escalate.
He reiterated that Moscow would resort to all weapons in its arsenal, including nuclear ones, if its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad was threatened.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russian forces strike Sloviansk with Smerch rockets: one killed, one injured.
Smerch rockets struck Sloviansk on 1 October, damaging at least 35 houses, killing a 26-year-old man and injuring a 66-year-old civilian.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Thousands in Kosovo Protest Again for ‘Fair Justice’ After Hague Convictions.
- Balkan Insight, 4 hours ago: Thousands in Kosovo Protest Again for ‘Fair Justice’ After Hague Convictions.
Large crowds attend rally in Pristina against Hague court verdict convicting four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders of war crimes, with protest speaker attacking 'double standards when it comes to justice'.
- Politico Europe, one hour ago: As Germany’s far right rises, weakened Merz looks to project strength and resolve against Putin.
In a closely watched speech, the chancellor sought to reassure worried allies in Europe and Ukraine while warning Germans to stay the course against Moscow, lest Russia’s war machine ‘turn against us.’
- Politico Europe, 4 hours ago: ‘We have not delivered’: Germany’s Wadephul criticizes slow EU enlargement progress.
Germany's foreign minister warns that Europe risks losing credibility in the Western Balkans.
- Balkan Insight, 10 hours ago: Bosnian Serb Wartime Leader Biljana Plavsic Dies Aged 96.
Wartime vice-president of Bosnia’s Serb-dominated entity, the only woman ever convicted of war crimes by the Hague Tribunal, dies in Belgrade – to the end maintaining she had 'done nothing wrong'.

- AllAfrica - Conflict, 10 hours ago: Mali: Who Wins From Ukraine's Drones in Mali?.
[African Arguments] On 12 September, CNN reported that around fifteen Ukrainian drone specialists are working with the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) in northern Mali. According to two Ukrainians deployed there, the group does not fight on the front line; it trains fighters and helps run operations. A Ukrainian operator told CNN that he coordinates the rebels' operations remotely and that Ukrainians helped take Kidal earlier this year. Hundreds of mourners in Gaza City held a vigil on Wednesday for 105 people killed during Israel's war on the Palestinian territory. Their bodies were recovered in the past several days, after remaining buried under the rubble for nearly three years.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 15 hours ago: Ethiopia: UN Warns Northern Ethiopia Escalation Threatens Civilians, Aid Operations.
[Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- The United Nations has raised fresh concerns over the rapidly evolving conflict in northern Ethiopia, warning that renewed fighting is exposing civilians, including people displaced by the previous war, to further protection risks while generating new displacement.

The conflict is also spreading beyond Tigray, with fighting reported in neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions. Communications remain disrupted, making independent verification of battlefield claims difficult.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: 'Everything necessary will be done': Military spokesman reaffirms Pakistan's right to self-defence against Afghanistan-based terrorism.
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, 3 hours ago: 'Everything necessary will be done': Military spokesman reaffirms Pakistan's right to self-defence against Afghanistan-based terrorism.
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said on Thursday that Pakistan had the right to self-defence and “everything that is necessary will be done” in response to terrorism emanating from Afghanistan. Pakistan has seen a surge in terrorism since the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) ended its ceasefire deal with the government in November 2022, vowing to increase attacks. In response, the government labelled the group as Fitna-al-Khawarij (FAK) and directed the use of the term khariji for attackers.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 14 hours ago: ‘Calibrated’ air strikes target terrorist hideouts at two locations in Afghanistan: info ministry.
Pakistan carried out “well-planned and calibrated” air strikes against terrorist hideouts in Afghanistan, the information ministry said on Thursday. In a post on X, the ministry said the strikes were carried out in continuation of Operation Ghazab lil Haq and Pakistan’s resolve to eliminate terrorists, their networks and supporters. It said the aerial strikes targeted the hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations it referred to as Fitna al Khwarij and Fitna al Hindustan, and resulted in the deaths of “multiple terrorists”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 3 hours ago: ‘Why the need for all this drama’: DG ISPR lampoons India's 'neutralised Pakistani terrorist' claims, presents him before media.
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry lampooned India’s claims of “neutralising” a “terrorist” allegedly linked to the Pakistani military, presenting the individual during a press conference on Thursday. The press briefing came after Indian media reported that an individual wanted in connection with the April 22 Pahalgam terrorist attack last year had been killed during an “encounter” in Indian Illegally Occupied Kashmir’s Korag area.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Saudi-led coalition says Houthis attacked power station in Madina.
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis said on Thursday the group had attacked a power distribution station in Madina this week, putting one transformer out of service but without affecting the electricity network. The coalition said an investigation and examination of drone wreckage confirmed Houthi involvement in planning and carrying out Tuesday’s attack. It said the station supplies electricity to the Prophet’s Mosque.
India - bottom line: ‘Fatal point of no return’: Putin warns against use of nukes amid global tensions.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: ‘Fatal point of no return’: Putin warns against use of nukes amid global tensions.
Vladimir Putin expressed concerns about current global tensions and the potential for disastrous outcomes from escalating conflicts. He emphasized the importance of preventing the use of weapons of mass destruction in international disputes. Putin highlighted the role of Western technical support in Ukraine's military actions against Russia. He stated that Russia is not planning attacks on European countries but would respond to any aggression.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Massachusetts couple wins $310,000 judgment in neighbour tree dispute.
A Massachusetts couple achieved a remarkable win in their legal battle against their neighbor, successfully advocating for themselves in court. They were awarded $310,000 for damages due to tree destruction and unauthorized encroachments. The ruling by the Massachusetts Appeals Court upheld their victory, emphasizing that self-represented individuals can indeed confront intricate legal issues effectively. This judgment concludes a drawn-out conflict over property rights and associated damages.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Iran military kills 6 in Zahedan, accuses armed groups of ties with foreign powers.
Iranian military forces killed six members of a designated terrorist group in Zahedan on Thursday. Clashes between security forces and armed groups frequently occur in Sistan-Baluchistan province, highlighting ongoing regional tensions. The Iranian revolutionary guards reported finding explosive packages with the detained individuals during their operation. Meanwhile, Tehran is contemplating the United States' response to its recent peace proposal for reviving negotiations.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Flydubai incident: Indian pilot stable, co-pilot in custody; Saudi, UAE launch probes.
On a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight, the Omani co-pilot allegedly attacked the captain in the cockpit. Indian captain Smit Machchhar sustained serious injuries but managed to unlock the cockpit door. Passengers intervened and overpowered the co-pilot, ensuring the safety of everyone aboard. The flight was diverted to Saudi Arabia, where all 174 people landed safely. Investigations by authorities from Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Israel are ongoing.
